newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares seen trading sideways next week.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares seen trading sideways next week.

text.p: Manila shares will trade sideways with an upward bias next week with slow buying in select blue chips and continued attention on small cap issues, traders said on Friday.
Helen Alvarez, research head of All Asia Securities, said news on Friday about Standard & Poor upgrading the Philippines foreign rating from BB to BB-plus will likely perk up Monday's session.

"But what's holding back investors is the political uncertainty. There will be some caution especially among foreign investors as long as the issue about charter change is in the background," said Raul Ruiz, vice-president at Sun Hung Kai Securities.
News this week that members of the ruling party were in favour of amending the Constitution to extend the term of the president caused some stir at the bourse.
The main index closed down on Friday by 8.45 points at 3,301.98 shedding 20.32 points, or 0.61 percent, to 3,322.30 week-on-week.
